headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to make large energy users, such as data centers, responsible for their own grid infrastructure costs, potentially reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocacy groups, residential ratepayers, Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia regulators make data centers pay for grid upgrades
news_summary: Virginia regulators are shifting the costs of power infrastructure upgrades to data centers to protect households and small businesses from higher utility bills. The State Corporation Commission has directed Dominion Energy to draft a policy requiring data centers to pay for certain grid improvements, especially for new substations or transmission lines built solely for their facilities.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency and data for environmental monitoring and water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Data Center Water Use
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed Senate Bill 553, sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, to strengthen water-use reporting requirements for data centers. This legislation aims to provide better data on water supplied to data centers, addressing concerns about the lack of centralized tracking as the industry expands.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill sets guidelines for where data centers can be built and limits the noise they produce, addressing community concerns and environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Siting Law
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, governs where large data centers can be sited and what developers must disclose before local approval. It requires site assessments for noise impacts on residential units and schools within 500 feet, and allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
